comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: Creating `LoggingService()` at import time introduces global side effects (and potential startup cost) even when the plugin/module isn’t used. Prefer deferring logger/service initialization to the plugin instance (e.g., inside `__init__`) or use a standard module logger that doesn’t require constructing a service during import.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: Logging the full `config` object can leak secrets (tokens, credentials, connection strings) into logs. Consider logging a redacted/safe subset (e.g., only relevant boolean flags, or a sanitized dict) and explicitly exclude known-sensitive keys.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: Logging `payload.args` is likely to include user-provided content and may contain PII/secrets; this is especially risky in a security-related component. Recommend logging only structural info (e.g., arg keys, counts) and/or redacting values before logging; if detailed debugging is needed, gate it behind an explicit opt-in setting for safe environments.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: These debug statements use f-strings, which eagerly stringify potentially large objects even when DEBUG logging is disabled. Prefer lazy formatting (e.g., `logger.debug(\"... %s\", value)`) or guard with `if logger.isEnabledFor(DEBUG): ...` to avoid unnecessary work on hot paths.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: Setting `LOG_LEVEL: DEBUG` for the server process in CI can significantly increase log volume and may expose sensitive data if any request/arg logging exists (including the newly added logs). Consider scoping DEBUG more narrowly (e.g., logger-specific level for `plugins.sql_sanitizer`) or ensuring the sanitizer logs are redacted before enabling DEBUG globally.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: The `cat ... | grep ...` check is fragile: it depends on log formatting including the substring `sql_sanitizer`, and it will fail the job if grep finds nothing (even if behavior is correct). Prefer grepping for a stable marker you control (e.g., the literal `SQL-SANITIZER`) using `grep -F`, and avoid the UUOC by calling grep directly; if the goal is informational, make the grep non-fatal or emit a clearer assertion/error message when missing.
